A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research on choice biases in language-model evaluation, despite the changed title and metric terminology. Their complete text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model evaluations across eight benchmark tasks, including prior-probability analyses, metric comparisons and the appended-'Hi' experiment in Appendix B.

after.justification: v4 reports original experiments on input formats, model scale, demonstrations, instructions and adversarial choices, with additional empirical analyses in Appendices C–E.

M1.justification: NPSQ retains ANPMI's normalized log-probability-shift formula, but changes its reference probability. v1 uses unconditional P(Choice), whereas v4 conditions on retained choice-related context C when removing question-related input Q. This changes scoring inputs, particularly for symbols and hybrid formats, while preserving the central normalization procedure.

E1.justification: Coverage contracts from eight benchmark tasks to HellaSwag, ARC-Challenge and MMLU. PiQA, ARC-Easy, LogiQA, RACE and SciQ evaluations disappear, including from the appendices. Meanwhile, v4 introduces instructional and neutral adversarial-choice scenarios beyond v1's appended-'Hi' test.

E2.justification: v1 Tables 2–3 compare ANPMI against raw likelihood, length normalization and unnormalized PMI, with label-frequency references in Table 2. v4 Figures 3–4 and 8 compare NPSQ only against raw and length-normalized likelihood. Removing PMI eliminates the closest comparator and the direct empirical comparison isolating the normalization step.

E3.justification: v1 uses zero-shot evaluations with benchmark-specific formats. v4 systematically varies cloze, symbols and hybrid formats, 0/1/5/10 demonstrations, task instructions and base versus instruction-tuned models. Qwen2.5 models spanning 0.5B–72B replace OPT/Gemma coverage. Length normalization changes from characters to tokens, and adversarial tests replace an incorrect option rather than append one. The retained datasets' evaluation splits and sizes remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v4 expands the simple 'Hi' diagnostic into four adversarial-choice tests comparing scoring methods, and adds systematic format, demonstration and instruction analyses. Correctness-by-component analysis, accuracy–sensitivity regression and adversarial-score distributions are also added. v1's no-prompt accuracy comparison, length–probability scatter analysis and two worked answer-selection cases are removed.

E5.justification: v4 newly specifies seed 1234 for demonstration sampling and reports Pearson correlation, a regression confidence band of 95% and kernel density estimates in Appendices C–D. v1 has no corresponding statistical reporting. Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty for its main accuracy results.

E6.justification: The result set is substantially replaced and expanded across experimental conditions. For example, v1 Table 5 reports 95.10% answer changes for LLaMA3.1-8B on HellaSwag after appending 'Hi'; v4 Section 5.1 reports 93.19% selection of a replacement simple adversary under raw likelihood and below 0.17% adversarial selection under NPSQ for simple/extended attacks. These are different protocols, not a same-setting performance improvement. v4 also adds format, instruction, demonstration and correctness-decomposition findings.

T1.justification: v1's extended derivations concerning PMI/NPMI symmetry, joint probabilities and normalization bounds are removed. v4 instead generalizes the existing top-two dominance criterion to a question/choice decomposition of scoring functions and derives the conditional probability-shift bound. The normalized-shift principle and zero score without the question persist, but the formal development changes substantially.

C1.justification: The central concern about choice biases remains. However, v4 elevates quantifying choice sensitivity across formats into a principal contribution and adds an explicit abstract/conclusion claim of robustness to modified answer options. This substantially broadens the contribution beyond v1's emphasis on correcting unconditional priors through ANPMI's equal-baseline and common-bound properties.

C2.justification: v4 interprets choice contributions as detrimental to cloze accuracy but beneficial in symbols/hybrid formats, and explains residual NPSQ sensitivity through interactions among choices, including Mistral failures in Appendix E. It also adds an accuracy–sensitivity interpretation. v1's explicit limitations concerning tasks where priors matter, non-MCQ applicability and extremely high choice priors are removed.

D1.justification: v4 supplies exact templates for all three formats, identifies their template source, diagrams the Q/C/input partition and explains retaining complete demonstrations when removing the target question. Table 1 specifies the adversarial strings. These substantially revise and extend v1's benchmark-specific Harness templates and provide important reproduction details for the new experiments.

R1.justification: v4 substantially expands positioning around prompt formatting, option ordering, demonstration sensitivity and evaluation reliability, adding works such as Alzahrani et al. (2024), Pezeshkpour and Hruschka (2024), Balepur and Rudinger (2024), and Molfese et al. (2025). It emphasizes formal quantification beyond observational artifact studies, while removing the PMI/NPMI literature discussion and associated foundational references.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and much of the main narrative are rewritten. ANPMI becomes NPSQ, and separate existing-metric/theoretical sections give way to a choice-sensitivity framework, organized observations and robustness experiments. The appendices are extensively reorganized, and the standalone limitations section disappears.

P2.justification: The two-column document becomes a single-column ICLR-style paper. v1's dense accuracy tables, probability-length plot, fairness schematic and worked-example panels are replaced by extensive multi-panel sensitivity and adversarial charts. v4 adds prompt tables, an input-format diagram, a component-decomposition table, regression and density plots, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v4 provides stronger direct evidence for robustness through controlled comparisons across attacks, formats and models, supported by clearer input specifications; v1's 'Hi' experiment did not test ANPMI robustness. These gains are tempered by removal of the PMI comparator, overly broad cloze-superiority and stability claims relative to Figures 4 and 8, and Appendix C's incorrect inference from observations outside a regression confidence band. The revision improves empirical validation, but does not establish that the metric measures true comprehension.
